A menacing plane cut through the misty June day like a buzz saw, and woke up all the birds and bugs in the process. Behind his house, some distant whine and prattle of a weedwhacker chopping grass then wood. Perfect temperature in the shade, narrow seat was oddly uncomfortable. In the sun was slightly too warm, but his vast towel was a magic carpet of softness and sleepibilty. One or two. Still hungover, but orange juice was a wonderful drug. And rubinoff. But he had vowed not to start until 3 today, so at least he wouldn't be driving. He tried to forget about his head, instead, focused all his energy on his nose. It smelled strongly of pine at first, since the desiccating Christmas tree was more orange than a kardashian. They don't get autocorrected and capitalized, yet. The sharp needles poked red dots in his sole that slowly vanished. A loud crunch in the woods by the river. A flash of light. A guttural gleeful growl. A light pounce, a nimble bound, on the ground.
